questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: It had to be a nice and affordable city with a good university and an opportunity to learn or practise a third language.

questions.answer: It was alright. The Erasmus Team at Freie responds really quickly to e-mails and are very helpful.

questions.answer: I attended some virtual info meetings with practical information. To me it was very helpful to be in contact with former exchange students.

questions.answer: Off campus

questions.answer: It can be really difficult to find housing in Berlin. WG Gesucht is normally where people find a room.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I highly recomment living off campus. I have only heard bad things about the student accomodation.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for courses during the first two weeks of the semester, so you can try different courses before you decide. It is super stressful and confusing, but you just have to be patient. In the end, everyone seems to get the courses they wish for.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They do an info meeting about the registration process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the courses I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience and don't stress about it. It will be fine in the end. Basically, you can just show up at the classes you find interesting and then ask the instructor if you may follow their class. I am sure they will say yes. Contact former exchange students for advice.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I would say that the level is in general quite high, although in a different way than at home. In terms of methods and research design, I think KU is quite stronger, but in terms of critical thinking and level of abstraction, Freie is very strong.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Critical engagement, active participation and open discussion plays a much bigger role which is super nice.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Global Tax Politics (7 ECTS) by Lukas Hakelberg
Banks and banking in global politics (3 ECTS) by Andrea Binder
Gqola, Hartman and Wynter – A South African – Afro-American -and Afro Caribbean Conversation on the Atlantic Slave (7 ECTS) by Sara Dehkordi
Quantitative Methods in Autocracy Research (3 ECTS) by Alexander Libman
Sociology of Conspiracy Theories (7 ECTS) by Philipp Wunderlich
Needs: Philosophical Perspectives (3 ECTS) by Robin Celikates

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would especially recommend courses from Lukas Hakelberg for those interested in IPE and Sara Dehkordi for those interested in postcolonial feminism. I also recommend trying a course at another faculty. I learned a lot from following Robin Celikates' philosophy course "Need: Philosophical Perspectives". I highly recommend not to follow the pre-semester German course (Vorkurs) - it was too expensive and very bad and stressful. There are many much cheaper and much better language schools which are also located in central Berlin, e.g. Speakeasy and die deutSCHule.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Enjoy Berlin of course (there is not enough space in the world for me to do a list of nice things to do in Berlin) and do day trips to Potsdam and all the nice lakes around Berlin (Schlachtensee, Krumme Lanke, Liepnitzsee, Wannsee). I also highly recommend taking a weekend in Prague which is only a cheap 4-5 hours bus ride away.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Germans have a very different perception of COVID-19. In Denmark, there were no restriction since 1 February, but in Germany we had to where masks in class during the whole semester.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Berlin clubbing culture :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Don't participate in the pre-semester German language course on Freie (Vorkurs). It is expensive, bad and far way. It is a good way to meet other exchange students, but there are other ways to meet them.
2) However, do use the opportunity to learn some German. The summer semester starts in April and the winter semester starts in end-October - so use February and March or September and October to go to a language school and follow an intensive German class. I can recommend Speakeasy in Friedrichshain and die deutSCHule in Neukölln.
3) Berlin is more than Kreuzberg and Neukölln - these areas are amazing and definitely where you wanna spend most of your time, but make sure to explore the rest of Berlin and its surroundings.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: If you are in Berlin during the spring, I recommend looking out for the annual Walter Benjamin Lectures in the end of June. This year, the guest was Nancy Fraser, and earlier guests have been Axel Honneth and Charles Taylor.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in beautiful and magical Berlin <3 <3 <3

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The fact that the semester goes from April to September/October, so I really recommend future students to get their exam papers done in August before the new semester at home begins.

questions.answer: Yes
